content_sanskrit: एवमत्याकुले युद्धे सास्फोटभयसंकुले । आदित्ये तमसा वृद्धे चटत्कठिनकङ्कटे
padaccheda: एवम् । अति । आकुले । सास्फोट-भय-संकुले । तमसा । आदित्ये । वृद्धे । चटत्-कठिन-कङ्कटे । युद्धे
anvaya: एवम् अति आकुले सास्फोट-भय-संकुले तमसा आदित्ये वृद्धे चटत्-कठिन-कङ्कटे युद्धे (सति)
meaning_english: In this way, the battle became extremely chaotic, filled with the sounds of slapping and terror. As the sun was obscured by rising darkness and hard armor pieces shattered loudly,

padaccheda: अम्बु-उत्पतन्तीषु । अश्म-वृष्टिषु । पतन्तीषु । क्षेपणात् । छासु । नदीषु । वहति । वरकेषु । अब्ज-पङ्क्तिषु
anvaya: अम्बु-उत्पतन्तीषु अश्म-वृष्टिषु पतन्तीषु क्षेपणात् छासु नदीषु वहति वरकेषु अब्ज-पङ्क्तिषु (इव च)
meaning_english: As stone-showers fell like rising waters and rivers flowed due to the discharge of missiles, the rows of shields appeared like clusters of lotuses.

content_sanskrit: मिथः फलाग्रकाटोत्थवह्निसीकरिणीषु च । आयान्तीषु प्रयान्तीषु दूरं शरनदीषु च
padaccheda: मिथः । फल-अग्र-कोट-उत्थ-वह्नि-सीकरिणीषु । च । दूरम् । आयान्तीषु । प्रयान्तीषु । शर-नदीषु । च
anvaya: मिथः फल-अग्र-कोट-उत्थ-वह्नि-सीकरिणीषु च दूरम् आयान्तीषु प्रयान्तीषु शर-नदीषु च (सतीषु)
meaning_english: Sparkling fires arose from the mutual clashing of the tips of weapon-points, while rivers of arrows traveled back and forth over great distances.
The ocean of the sky was filled by celestial rivers of weapon-crowds, undulating with whirlpools formed by the severed, floating heads that resembled lotuses.
The dense clouds, filled with weapons making a whistling sound in the wind, caused irritation to the Siddhas at the horizon, like the stinging pain of Kapikacchu seeds.

padaccheda: अष्ट-भाग-दशा-शेष-प्रताप-मधुर-आकृति । वीरः । इव । अहः । शस्त्र-घात-ओजसा । तनुताम् । ययौ
anvaya: अष्ट-भाग-दशा-शेष-प्रताप-मधुर-आकृति वीरः इव अहः शस्त्र-घात-ओजसा तनुताम् ययौ
meaning_english: The day, having only an eighth part remaining and possessing a gentle form of diminished heat, reached thinness like a warrior exhausted by the power of weapon-strikes.

content_sanskrit: श्रान्ताश्वेभाः प्रभग्नाश्च हेतिसंघातदीप्तयः । दिवसेन समं सेना ययुर्मन्दप्रतापताम्
padaccheda: श्रान्त-अश्व-इभाः । प्रभग्नाः । च । हेति-संघात-दीप्तयः । सेनाः । दिवसेन । समम् । मन्द-प्रतापताम् । ययुः
anvaya: श्रान्त-अश्व-इभाः प्रभग्नाः च हेति-संघात-दीप्तयः सेनाः दिवसेन समम् मन्द-प्रतापताम् ययुः
meaning_english: With exhausted horses and elephants, and the brilliance of the mass of weapons shattered, the armies reached a state of diminished glory along with the fading day.

content_sanskrit: अथसेनाधिनाथाभ्यां विचार्य सहमन्त्रिभिः । दूताः परस्परं वृत्ता युद्धं संह्रियतामिति
padaccheda: अथ । सेना-अधिनाथाभ्याम् । मन्त्रिभिः । सह । विचार्य । परस्परम् । दूताः । वृत्ताः । युद्धम् । संह्रियताम् । इति
anvaya: अथ सेना-अधिनाथाभ्यां मन्त्रिभिः सह विचार्य परस्परं दूताः वृत्ताः युद्धम् संह्रियताम् इति
meaning_english: Then, the two army commanders, having consulted with their ministers, dispatched messengers to one another with the instruction that the battle should be withdrawn.

padaccheda: तत्र । श्रम-वशात् । मन्द-यन्त्र-शस्त्र-पराक्रमैः । सर्वैः । एव । काले । रण-संहरणम् । उररीकृतम्
anvaya: तत्र श्रम-वशात् मन्द-यन्त्र-शस्त्र-पराक्रमैः सर्वैः एव काले रण-संहरणम् उररीकृतम्
meaning_english: There, due to fatigue and the slowing prowess of machines and weapons, the cessation of battle at that time was accepted by everyone.

content_sanskrit: ततो महारथोत्तुङ्गकेतुप्रान्तकृतास्पदम् । बलयोरारुहोहैक एको योधो ध्रुवो यथा
padaccheda: ततः । महा-रथ-उत्तुङ्ग-केतु-प्रान्त-कृत-आस्पदम् । बलयोः । एकः । एकः । योधः । ध्रुवः । यथा । आरुरोह
anvaya: ततः महा-रथ-उत्तुङ्ग-केतु-प्रान्त-कृत-आस्पदम् बलयोः एकः एकः योधः ध्रुवः यथा आरुरोह
meaning_english: Then, one by one, the warriors ascended their stations near the tall banners of their great chariots, standing firm like the pole star (Dhruva).

content_sanskrit: सोंऽशुकं भ्रामयामास सर्वदिङ्मण्डले सितम् । श्यामेव दीर्घशुद्धांशुं युद्धं संह्रियतामिति
padaccheda: सः । युद्धम् । संह्रियताम् । इति । सर्व-दिक्-मण्डले । सितम् । अंशुकम् । भ्रामयामास । इव । श्यामा । दीर्घ-शुद्ध-अंशुम्
anvaya: सः (राजा) युद्धं संह्रियताम् इति सर्व-दिक्-मण्डले सितम् अंशुकम् (तथा) भ्रामयामास इव श्यामा (रात्रिः) दीर्घ-शुद्ध-अंशुं (भ्रामयति) ।
meaning_english: He waved a white cloth across all directions as a signal for the battle to end, resembling the dark night spreading its long and pure rays of moonlight.

content_sanskrit: ततो दुन्दुभयो नेदुः प्रतिध्वनितदिङ्मुखाः । महाप्रलयसंशान्तौ पुष्करावर्तका इव
padaccheda: ततः । प्रतिध्वनित-दिक्-मुखाः । दुन्दुभयः । महा-प्रलय-संशान्तौ । पुष्कर-आवर्तकाः । इव । नेदुः
anvaya: ततः प्रतिध्वनित-दिक्-मुखाः दुन्दुभयः महा-प्रलय-संशान्तौ पुष्कर-आवर्तकाः इव नेदुः ।
meaning_english: Then, the war-drums resounded, echoing through the quarters of the sky, like the clouds of universal dissolution (puṣkarāvartaka) rumbling at the conclusion of the great cataclysm.

content_sanskrit: शरादिहेतिसरितो विस्तीर्णे गगने स्थिते । प्रवृत्ताः सुखमागन्तुं सरसः सरितो यथा
padaccheda: गगने । स्थिते । विस्तीर्णे । शर-आदि-हेति-सरितः । प्रवृत्ताः । यथा । सरसः । सरितः । सुखम् । आगन्तुम्
anvaya: गगने स्थिते विस्तीर्णे शर-आदि-हेति-सरितः (तथा) प्रवृत्ताः यथा सरसः सरितः सुखम् आगन्तुं (प्रवृत्ताः) ।
meaning_english: The rivers of arrows and weapons that had filled the vast sky began to subside, just as rivers flow peacefully back into a lake.

content_sanskrit: योधदोर्द्रुमसंचारस्तनुतामाययौ शनैः । भूकम्पान्ते वनस्पन्द इवाभ्रान्त इवार्णवः
padaccheda: योध-दोः-द्रुम-संचारः । भू-कम्प-अन्ते । वन-स्पन्दः । इव । अभ्रान्तः । अर्णवः । इव । शनैः । तनुताम् । आययौ
anvaya: योध-दोः-द्रुम-संचारः भू-कम्प-अन्ते वन-स्पन्दः इव अभ्रान्तः अर्णवः इव शनैः तनुताम् आययौ ।
meaning_english: The movement of the warriors' tree-like arms gradually diminished, like the swaying of a forest after an earthquake or the ocean becoming still after a storm.

content_sanskrit: विनिर्गन्तुं प्रववृते रणादथ बलद्वयम् । वारिपूरश्चतुर्दिक्षु प्रलयैकार्णवादिव
padaccheda: अथ । बल-द्वयम् । प्रलय-एक-अर्णवाद् । वारि-पूरः । इव । रणात् । चतुर्-दिक्षु । विनिर्गन्तुम् । प्रववृते
anvaya: अथ बल-द्वयम् प्रलय-एक-अर्णवाद् वारि-पूरः इव रणात् चतुर्-दिक्षु विनिर्गन्तुं प्रववृते ।
meaning_english: Then, the two armies began to depart from the battlefield in all four directions, like the receding floodwaters of the single ocean at the end of a kalpa.

padaccheda: उत्क्षिप्त-मन्दर-क्षीर-समुद्र-वत् । अनाकुलम् । सैन्यम् । प्रशाम्यद्-आवर्तम् । शनैः । साम्यम् । उपाययौ
anvaya: उत्क्षिप्त-मन्दर-क्षीर-समुद्र-वत् अनाकुलम् सैन्यम् प्रशाम्यद्-आवर्तं शनैः साम्यम् उपाययौ ।
meaning_english: The army, which had been as agitated as the ocean of milk churned by Mount Mandara, gradually attained tranquility as its whirlpools of commotion subsided.

padaccheda: क्रमेण । मुहूर्तेन । विकट-उदर-भीषणम् । रणाङ्गणम् । अगस्त्य-पीत-अर्णव-वत् । शून्यम् । एव । आसीत्
anvaya: क्रमेण मुहूर्तेन विकट-उदर-भीषणम् रणाङ्गणम् अगस्त्य-पीत-अर्णव-वत् शून्यम् एव आसीत् ।
meaning_english: Gradually, within an hour, the battlefield, though terrifying with its grisly interior, became empty like the ocean after it was swallowed by the sage Agastya.
Filled with heaps of corpses and agitated by flowing rivers of blood, the field resembled a forest teeming with the chirping and buzzing of crickets.
The field echoed with the gurgling sound of waves in the flowing streams of blood and was filled with the frantic cries of the living and the moans of the half-dead calling out.
Cascades of blood flowed from the heaps of dead and dying bodies, creating the illusion that the corpses were moving when they were actually resting on the backs of those still alive.
The battlefield featured fragments of clouds resting atop heaps of elephant carcasses; it was filled with masses of shattered chariots and resembled a great forest uprooted by a violent wind.
Horses and elephants were being swept away by the force of flowing rivers of blood, and the area was crowded with arrows, spears, double-edged swords, clubs, maces, darts, and swords.
The ground was covered with saddles, protective equipment, and armor; the bodies of the dead were hidden under a multitude of banners, fly-whisks, and silk cloths.
The wind whistled through the hollows of quivers that looked like expanded hoods of serpents, while piśācas slept on beds made of heaps of straw-like corpses.
The battlefield was covered by a forest of rainbows formed by the glitter of crowns, necklaces, and armlets; long ropes of thick intestines were being dragged by the paws of dogs and jackals.
The blood-soaked field was bristling with barely living men moaning in pain, while survivors resembled frogs submerged in the mud of gore.
Hundreds of bulging eyeballs peered through holes in excellent armor, and hundreds of terrible rivers of blood carried away heaps of severed arms and thighs like logs of wood.
The field was surrounded by wailing kinsmen amidst the dead and the dying; the spaces were filled with arrows, weapons, chariots, horses, elephants, and saddles.
The sky seemed bowed down by the circle of staff-like arms of dancing headless trunks, and the nostrils were pained and moistened by the stench of rut, marrow, and fat.
The ebbing lives of dying elephants and horses were being blocked by their own heaving gasps, while the war-drums were being struck by the lapping waves of the flowing rivers of blood.
Hundreds of rivers of blood flowed, carrying away dead elephants, horses, and crocodiles. Channels of blood spurted out with gurgling sounds from the gasping mouths of the dying army of men.

The faces and eyes of those with little life remaining were filled with arrows, their luster and voices fading. The air was thick with the stench of flesh, fat, and marrow, as gushing blood overflowed in every direction.

Truncated bodies were being trampled by the trunks of dying lordly elephants with upturned nostrils. High-piled headless corpses were being knocked down by riderless horses and elephants wandering aimlessly.
The battlefield surged with waves of blood agitated by the falling corpses of those wailing and screaming. Noble women gave up their lives by the sword, falling upon the necks of their dead husbands.
The field was scattered with many travelers quickly examining the fallen ranks of the army. It was crowded with living followers being dragged away by the hands of those removing the dead bodies.
Hundreds of rivers formed where hair resembled moss and faces looked like lotus-whirlpools. Great rivers of blood flowed, filled with high, surging waves of the fallen.

Half-dead men were preoccupied with pulling out weapons embedded in their limbs. Cries arose for the elephants and horses that had perished in a foreign land, their bodies offered like oblations in the sacrifice of war.

At the end of their lives, the dying called upon their sons, beloved ones, mothers, and gods. The air was filled with cries of "hā-hā" and "hī-hī," expressing the excruciating pain of their vital organs being pierced.
The dying heaps of the most powerful enemies lay accumulated. Those unable to withstand the elephant charge died with the names of their favorite deities on their lips.
While some died with great disdain for the enemy, even heroes were forced to flee. Many were driven by desperation into the terrifying whirlpools of blood that appeared unexpectedly.
The battlefield appeared like an assault of Vetāla faces begun by a multitude of headless trunks, where the agony of arrow strikes piercing vital organs made one's past sins manifest.

padaccheda: उह्यमान-ध्वज-छत्र-चारु-चामर-पङ्कजम् । किरत् । सन्ध्या-अरुणम् । दिक्षु । तेजस्कम् । रक्त-पङ्कजम्
anvaya: (तत्) उह्यमान-ध्वज-छत्र-चारु-चामर-पङ्कजम् दिक्षु सन्ध्या-अरुणम् तेजस्कम् रक्त-पङ्कजम् किरत् (आसीत्) ।
meaning_english: It bore beautiful whisks, umbrellas, and banners resembling lotuses being carried away, scattering a bloody mire in all directions that glowed with the brilliance of a crimson sunset.

padaccheda: रथ-चक्र-धर-आवर्तम् । रक्त-अर्णवम् । इव । अष्टमम् । पताका-फेन-पुञ्ज-आढ्यम् । चारु-चामर-बुद्बुदम्
anvaya: (तत्) रथ-चक्र-धर-आवर्तम् पताका-फेन-पुञ्जा-आढ्यम् चारु-चामर-बुद्बुदम् अष्टमम् रक्त-अर्णवम् इव (आसीत्) ।
meaning_english: Like an eighth ocean of blood, it swirled with chariot wheels for whirlpools, was thick with foam-like banners, and featured beautiful yak-tail fans as its bubbles.

padaccheda: विपर्यस्त-रथम् । भूमि-पङ्क-मग्न-पुर-उपमम् । उत्पात-वात-निर्धूत-द्रुमम् । वनम् । इव । आततम्
anvaya: (तत्) विपर्यस्त-रथम् भूमि-पङ्क-मग्न-पुर-उपमम् उत्पात-वात-निर्धूत-द्रुमम् आततम् वनम् इव (आसीत्) ।
meaning_english: With overturned chariots, it resembled a city submerged in the mire of the earth or an expansive forest whose trees had been uprooted by a catastrophic gale.

padaccheda: कल्प-दग्ध-जगत्-प्रख्यम् । मुनि-पीत-अर्णव-उपमम् । अति-वृष्टि-हतम् । देशम् । इव । प्रोज्झित-मानवम्
anvaya: (तत्) कल्प-दग्ध-जगत्-प्रख्यम् मुनि-पीत-अर्णव-उपमम् अति-वृष्टि-हतम् प्रोज्झित-मानवम् देशम् इव (आसीत्) ।
meaning_english: The scene resembled the world burnt at the end of a Kalpa, or the ocean swallowed by the sage Agastya, or a region devastated by torrential rains and abandoned by all human beings.
It was encircled by bundles of spears and crowded with circles of bhuśuṇḍī weapons, filled with corpses, javelins, and mallets that took the form of hundreds of intoxicated elephants.
Extensive like a grove of palm trees grown on rocky peaks, it featured tall spear-trees standing on the banks of rivers of flowing blood.
The field was crowded with flowery rays from weapon-trees fixed in the shoulders of elephants, while the sky was webbed with the tongue-like clusters of entrails dragged by vultures.
Tall forest-trees of spears grew on the banks of blood-rivers, and groups of banner-lotuses stood tall above the lakes of gore.
Men sinking in the bloody mud called out to their kinsmen, while survivors emerging from the falling carcasses of great elephants were gazed upon by others.

anvaya: हेति-लून-लतैः वृक्षैः संदिग्ध-अर्ध-कबन्धकम् असृक्-नदी-वहत्-हस्ति-कटक-कर्पट-नौ-गणम् (तत् युद्धम् अभवत्)
meaning_english: The battlefield was filled with trees whose creepers were severed by weapons, making them resemble headless torsos. It featured rivers of blood carrying hosts of elephant-blankets and torn garments, which appeared like fleets of boats.
White garments fluttering in the streams of blood looked like masses of foam. The field was crowded with an unending stream of men and swift attendants moving fixedly through the carnage.

anvaya: इतः च इतः च निपतत्-कबन्ध-रव-दानवम् ऊर्ध्व-स्थूल-अक्ष-चक्र-ओघ-छिन्न-सैन्य-द्रवत्-जनम् (तत् युद्धम् अभवत्)
meaning_english: The battle resounded with the noise of headless trunks falling here and there like demons. People fled as the army was sliced by a barrage of large, high-flying wheels and axles.
The air was filled with the gurgling of blood, howling, and the cries of the half-dead. Streams of blood flowing from the points of arrows (śilāmukha) washed away the dust and grounded the birds.
The field was congested with the frantic rhythmic dancing of towering Vetālas. Brave soldiers lay half-hidden within the broken wooden fragments of overturned chariots.
Throbbinng chariots containing living but trapped soldiers inspired terror. The sight of nearly dead warriors, their mouths filled with bloody mud, evoked a shadow of pity.

Dying men with uplifted necks watched dogs and crows in agony. The scene was chaotic with the din of carnivores fighting over single pieces of flesh, and crowded with scavengers who died while competing for the same prey.

content_sanskrit: विवृत्तासंख्याश्वद्विरदपुरुषाधीश्वररथप्रकृत्तोष्ट्रग्रीवाप्रसृतरुधिरोद्गारसुसरित् । रणोद्यानं मृत्योस्तदभवदशुष्कायुधलतं सशैलं कल्पान्ते जगदिव विपर्यस्तमखिलम्
padaccheda: विवृत्त-असंख्या-अश्व-द्विरद-पुरुष-अधीश्वर-रथ-प्रकृत्त-उष्ट्र-ग्रीवा-प्रसृत-रुधिर-उद्गार-सुसरित् । रण-उद्यानम् । मृत्योः । तत् । अभवत् । अशुष्क-आयुध-लतम् । स-शैलम् । कल्प-अन्ते । जगत् । इव । विपर्यस्तम् । अखिलम्
anvaya: विवृत्त-असंख्या-अश्व-द्विरद-पुरुष-अधीश्वर-रथ-प्रकृत्त-उष्ट्र-ग्रीवा-प्रसृत-रुधिर-उद्गार-सुसरित् तत् रण-उद्यानम् अशुष्क-आयुध-लतम् मृत्युः अभवत् कल्प-अन्ते सशैलम् विपर्यस्तम् अखिलम् जगत् इव
meaning_english: With great rivers of blood gushing from the severed necks of countless horses, elephants, men, kings, and camels, that battlefield became the garden of Death. Filled with 'creepers' of unsheathed weapons, it resembled the entire world overturned at the end of a Kalpa, including its mountains.
